_readme: Single source of truth for the NPV models. The Python engine (04_npv_engine.py) and the Excel workbook are both built from these values, and 05_reconcile_python_to_excel.py proves they produce the same results to the cent. Every value has a documented basis in config/assumption_basis.json (rendered as docs/ASSUMPTION_BASIS.md): S = statute or regulation, P = published industry or regulatory source, E = the kit's synthetic experience (zero credibility where the experience is synthetic, ASOP 25 §3.3), J = actuarial judgment with a stated range and a sensitivity in output/npv_judgment_sensitivity.csv. They are NOT Humana assumptions; in production this file is regenerated by the assumption-setting step from Humana's approved experience studies and must match an entry in config/assumption_approvals.json before the engine will run. Rates are annual unless noted.

features._readme: Model features. Setting every v3 flag to false reproduces version 2 exactly; the v4 flags (medicaid_contract_terms, dv_benefit_categories, mc_process_risk, mc_management_response) are each neutral at their neutral settings and are tested to reproduce v3 (tests/test_v4_model.py). The shipped Medicaid contract terms are not all neutral (2% quality withhold, v4.1).

profit_test._readme: After-tax distributable-earnings layer on top of the cash-flow projection. Claims are paid with the lag pattern of each line, claim reserves and the Medicaid MLR remittance liability are held until paid, required capital is held as a percentage of annualized paid claims (so it runs off with the claim reserve), assets earn the investment rate, and income is taxed at the IRC §11 rate. v4.1: the IRC §848 DAC tax is applied by line (dac_tax_rate_by_line: capitalize the rate x net premiums each tax year, deduct over 180 months with the half-year convention); it is a timing cost. Tax losses are assumed to be used against other company income. Basis: config/assumption_basis.json (tax S, investment rate P, capital P/J). In production capital comes from Humana's capital allocation and tax from Corporate Tax.

MEDSUPP.label: Medicare Supplement (Plan G, attained-age rated, underwritten, issue age 65)

antiselection._readme: Two health classes. 'Shoppers' can pass underwriting elsewhere; at each rate increase they are shopper_shock_lapse_propensity times as likely as non-shoppers to take the extra (shock) lapse. The split is solved each anniversary so the block's total lapse still equals base + shock from the lapse study (while the shopper rate stays below 100%, which holds in every scenario run here; the engine warns otherwise). Base lapse and mortality apply equally to both. Claim-cost relativities are set at issue and average 1.0, so year-1 claims are unchanged; as shoppers leave faster, the remaining block's average cost rises. Judgment values: the synthetic experience cannot measure this, and in production it is calibrated from post-rate-increase claims A/E.

dynamic_shock_lapse._readme: Shock lapse moves with the size of the rate increase: shock = max(0, shock_lapse_add_from_year2 + slope x (rate increase - reference)). At the reference increase the base shock is unchanged.

model_points._readme: v4 new-business portfolio: the base cell (Plan G, issue age 65) is one of several model points. mix = share of new issues by issue-age band and plan, and issue_age = mean issue age in the band: both READ OFF the synthetic book's 2024-2025 issues (Plan F excluded, see below) as a sales-mix placeholder for the Humana sales plan, disclosed in docs/ASSUMPTION_BASIS.md ('Values linked to the synthetic book'). They do not affect the headline Plan G cell; per-cell results are reported, so any mix is a weighted sum. Plan relativities scale year-1 premium and claim cost (P: published 2026 Maryland Med Supp rates, Plan N 0.77 and HDG 0.18 of Plan G; claim relativities set equal to premium relativities, i.e. the same loss ratio by plan; in production from Humana's filed rate relativities and morbidity study). Older issue ages start at the attained-age premium and claim cost: x (1 + premium_age_step)^(age - 65) and x (1 + claim_age_slope)^(age - 65). Plan F is excluded from NEW business: since 2020 it cannot be sold to people newly eligible for Medicare (MACRA), so new F sales are limited to people eligible before 2020 and are not a growth segment; the synthetic book's F issues at 65 in 2024-25 are not realistic and are not used. Lapse, selection, anti-selection, mortality slope and expenses per policy are the base-cell assumptions (no experience basis for differences by age or plan on this book).

benefit_categories._readme: v4 benefit-level claim cost. cost_share = share of ultimate claim cost by category, READ OFF the synthetic book's paid claims by service_category (2022-2025; sums to 1) as a placeholder, disclosed in docs/ASSUMPTION_BASIS.md; with neutral category settings it has no effect on the base results. trend_add_on = category trend minus the line trend (J; 0 because the experience cannot separate category trends over four years). pent_up_relativity = category year-1 pent-up relative to the line factor, normalized so the share-weighted year-1 factor equals first_year_pent_up_factor (J; 1.0 = uniform). waiting_period_months = no benefit before this policy month (product design, X; 0 = none, which is what the experience reflects); a waited category's pent-up load is deferred to its first 12 months of eligibility (v4.1). Neutral settings reproduce the single-category v3 model; the categories exist so product designs (e.g. a 12-month waiting period on MAJOR) and category trends can be tested.

MEDICAID.label: Medicaid managed care contract (new state launch)

rate_cells._readme: Rate cells for the new state. Shares are the starting and joiner membership mix. Each cell's capitation = blended capitation x capitation_relativity; each cell's medical cost = its capitation x the blended medical cost ratio x loss_ratio_relativity (a LOSS-RATIO relativity, not a cost relativity: a state data book's cost relativity must be divided by the cell's capitation relativity before it is entered here). The engine normalizes so the blended year-1 capitation, medical cost ratio and disenrollment equal the contract-level assumptions above (the levers the tornado and Monte Carlo shock). Capitation relativities: consistent with MACPAC per-enrollee spending by eligibility group (public). Member mix: READ OFF the synthetic book as a placeholder for the state data book (disclosed in docs/ASSUMPTION_BASIS.md); with churn differing by cell the mix matters (swept against the MACPAC national mix). Loss-ratio relativities are 1.0 (judgment, swept). Disenrollment relativities are MACPAC's 12-month churn by eligibility group, children 19%, adults 28%, disabled 9%, each divided by MACPAC's all-enrollee 21% (public, v4.3); the engine normalizes them to the 25% blend; equal churn by cell is swept as the alternative. In production they come from the state's rate certification and data book.

risk_adjustment._readme: Budget-neutral risk adjustment: the plan's medical cost scales with its acuity relative to the state average, and capitation moves by revenue_capture x (acuity - 1). Base acuity is 1.0 (neutral); the tornado tests +/-3%.

contract_terms._readme: v4 state contract terms (X in production: from the state contract and rate certification). v4.1 public basis: a 2% quality withhold with 85% expected earn-back (Louisiana rate certification and quality review; 42 CFR 438.6), the only non-neutral term; no acuity path, no directed payments and the MLR floor rule, because these are contract-specific. With every term at its neutral value (acuity 1, withhold 0, directed payments 0, rule floor) the model reproduces v3 exactly (tests/test_v4_model.py). acuity_shift.medical_factor_by_year multiplies medical cost by contract year (e.g. [1.0, 1.04, 1.03] for a post-redetermination acuity shift; years not listed = 1.0) and risk adjustment recognizes revenue_capture x (factor - 1) risk_adjustment_lag_years later. quality_withhold: withhold_pct of capitation held back, expected_earn_back share earned back and received six months after the year. directed_payments: pass-through PMPM in revenue and medical (in the MLR numerator and denominator). mlr_rule.type 'floor' (remit max(0, mlr_floor x revenue - medical)) or 'corridor' (symmetric risk corridor, parameters below).

monte_carlo._readme: Parameter-uncertainty Monte Carlo. Each draw is a level shift held for the whole projection. The Med Supp rate driver is the deviation of the approved increase from the assumed one, defined as assumed minus approved and symmetric (the assumption is the expected approval, so approvals land above it as often as below); its correlation with trend is therefore negative. v4 adds year-to-year process risk (process_risk) on top of the level shifts, and an explicit Med Supp / D&V rate-filing response to emerging trend (management_response), which replaces the v3 trend / Med Supp rate-shortfall correlation (set to 0 below).

correlations._readme: Correlations between the standard-normal drivers (used when correlated_monte_carlo is on). Positive trend-to-rate correlations mean rate actions partly follow emerging trend; the Med Supp rate driver is the shortfall, so its correlation with trend is negative. Judgment values. v4: the trend / Med Supp rate-shortfall correlation (-0.5 in v3) is 0 because the explicit filing response (management_response) now models how Med Supp rates follow trend; keeping both would count the effect twice.

process_risk._readme: v4 year-to-year volatility (J: calibrate with estimate_mc_parameters.py on Humana's history). Trend: stationary AR(1) deviation shared by all lines. Approval and Medicaid update noise: independent each year. Separate random stream (seed + seed_offset).

management_response._readme: v4 partial-adjustment rate-filing response (J): each filing closes gap_closure_per_filing of the claim-index deviation visible in experience lag_years old, less the premium deviation already in force. Calibrate from the rate-filing and approval history (requested vs approved vs indicated).
